scope: Theorem 2.2 (Tree inequality) of the manuscript “Path selection and an elliptic inequality on degenerating Ricci-flat trees” (preprints/Path-selection-and-an-elliptic-inequality-on-degenerating-Ricci-flat-trees-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 351 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a49f3dc92b22b888), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite rooted tree with the end identifications and order-20 metric bounds of Section 2.1. Let (gj, L(j), Mj) satisfy the compact vertex convergence, the same uniform half-end and root-end bounds, and Equation (2.3) through order 10, with every L (j) e → ∞ and Mj → 0. Then, in physical root units, E(gj) = o(Mj). (2.6) For an index with Mj = 0, the assertion means E(gj) = 0. The little-oh is taken for this fixed tree; it does not assert a power exponent uniform over different trees.
